pois.name: Ozeaneum
pois.blurb: Ozeaneum is a public aquarium in the German city of Stralsund. It is a main attraction of the German Oceanographic Museum (Deutsches Meeresmuseum), arguably one of the three largest institutions of its kind in Europe.

themeConnection.text: A permanent public aquarium and marine-life complex at a specific site in Stralsund.

pois.name: Aquarium de Paris
pois.blurb: The Trocadéro (pronounced [tʁɔkadeʁo] ), site of the Palais de Chaillot, is an area of Paris, France, in the 16th arrondissement, across the Seine from the Eiffel Tower.

image.attribution: Yortw from Auckland, New Zealand · CC BY 2.0

themeConnection.text: An individually named permanent public aquarium beneath the Trocadéro gardens in Paris.

pois.name: L'Oceanogràfic
pois.blurb: L'Oceanogràfic is an oceanarium in Valencia, Spain, designed as a large marine park with representations of major marine ecosystems.

themeConnection.text: A permanent public oceanarium complex in Valencia devoted primarily to aquatic ecosystems and animals.

pois.name: Nausicaá
pois.blurb: Boulogne-sur-Mer (French: [bulɔɲ syʁ mɛʁ] ; Picard: Boulonne-su-Mér; Dutch: Bonen; Latin: Gesoriacum or Bononia), often called just Boulogne (UK: , US: ), is a port city in Northern France.

themeConnection.text: A permanent public national sea centre and oceanarium in the incorporated city of Boulogne-sur-Mer.

pois.name: Georgia Aquarium

pois.name: The Dallas World Aquarium

pois.name: Aquarium Finisterrae

themeConnection.text: A permanent public aquarium in A Coruña displaying Atlantic marine life and aquatic ecosystems.

theme.title: Public Aquariums in Cities
theme.introduction: Dive into the public aquariums and oceanariums that bring marine life into cities worldwide.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named, permanent public aquarium, oceanarium, or aquarium complex whose principal visitor function is displaying living aquatic animals or aquatic ecosystems; (2) it has regularly scheduled public admission on the date of play, whether ticketed or free; (3) the named aquarium occupies a specific permanent site that can be pinned as one exact map location; (4) that site lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (5) the institution is operating under its own identifiable name, rather than being merely an unnamed exhibit within another attraction.
